```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
knitr::knit_hooks$set(inline = function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) x <- format(x, big.mark = ",")
  paste(x, collapse = ", ")
})
```

A Proteome Discoverer export has two columns that a conversion specification
can use as the intensity: `Intensity`, a single precursor signal, and
`Precursor Area`, the integrated peak area. Both look plausible to a language
model. This vignette shows a conversion specification that chose `Intensity`,
how to change it to `Precursor Area`, and what the choice does to the
differential abundance analysis. The conversion specification and the results
of the analysis were obtained once and saved, so the vignette runs without a
language model or the full export.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(MSstatsConvertLLM)
library(data.table)
```

# The export

We use the Proteome Discoverer output of PXD005642, a controlled mixture in
which proteins are spiked in known amounts into a constant *E. coli*
background. We distribute the rows of the export that the model was shown.
The benchmark of the manuscript normalized the column names before showing
them to the model, replacing spaces and other characters by dots, and the
conversion specification uses these names.

```{r export}
case <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "pd_case_study.rds",
                            package = "MSstatsConvertLLM"))
export <- normalize_headers(case$rows)
export[, .(Protein.Group.Accessions, Sequence, Charge, Intensity,
           Precursor.Area)]
```

# Inferring the conversion specification

`infer_specification()` sends the model the column names and the first
`r formals(infer_specification)$n_preview` rows of the export. We obtained the
saved conversion specification with the call below, using llama3.1-8b and the
constrained_v3 prompt, in the benchmark of the manuscript.

```{r infer-live, eval = FALSE}
specification <- infer_specification(export, "llama3.1-8b", "constrained_v3",
                                     acquisition = "DDA")
```

Here, we read the saved conversion specification instead.

```{r infer-saved}
specification <- case$specification
as.data.frame(specification$mappings)[, c("field", "from", "confidence")]
```

# Checking the intensity column

The model chose `Intensity`. In the example rows, both `Intensity` and
`Precursor.Area` are positive numbers, so neither looks wrong on its own. They
do not measure the same quantity, though: their ratio changes from row to row.

```{r candidates}
export[, .(Intensity, Precursor.Area,
           ratio = round(Precursor.Area / Intensity))]
```

`Intensity` is a single precursor signal, recorded for each match, while
`Precursor Area` is the integrated area of the precursor's peak. The
hand-written converter, `PDtoMSstatsFormat()`, reads `Precursor Area` unless
told otherwise.

```{r converter-default}
formals(MSstatsConvert::PDtoMSstatsFormat)$which.quantification
```

The converter can also read `Intensity`, so the gold standard of the benchmark
accepts it, and the benchmark counted this choice as correct.

```{r gold-standard}
GROUND_TRUTH$proteome_discoverer$Intensity
```

# Changing the conversion specification

The mappings are a data frame, so you can change the intensity column before
converting. Check that the new column exists in the export.

```{r fix}
fixed <- specification
fixed$mappings$from[fixed$mappings$field == "Intensity"] <- "Precursor.Area"
as.data.frame(fixed$mappings)[fixed$mappings$field == "Intensity",
                              c("field", "from")]
"Precursor.Area" %in% names(export)
```

# Differential abundance results

We converted the full export with the hand-written converter, which reads
`Precursor Area`, and with the LLM-based converter and the model's conversion
specification, which reads `Intensity`. We then analyzed both with MSstats, as
below. The script `compare_pxd005642.R` in the GitHub repository of the
package runs these steps.

```{r analysis-live, eval = FALSE}
export <- fread("ControlMixture_DDA_ProteomeDiscoverer_input.csv")
annotation <- fread("annotation.csv")

converted <- list(
  hand = MSstatsConvert::PDtoMSstatsFormat(export, annotation = annotation),
  llm  = LLMtoMSstatsFormat(normalize_headers(export), annotation = annotation,
                            llm_mapping = specification))
processed <- lapply(converted, MSstats::dataProcess,
                    normalization = "equalizeMedians",
                    featureSubset = "topN", n_top_feature = 3)
# contrast: one row for each pair of mixtures in which every spiked protein
# changes in amount
compared <- lapply(processed, function(p) MSstats::groupComparison(contrast, p))
```

Here, we read the saved results instead. They have one row per protein and
comparison. For each converter, they give the adjusted p-value, `adjp_h` for
the hand-written converter and `adjp_l` for the LLM-based converter, and
whether the protein was called significant, `sig_h` and `sig_l`. `spiked`
marks the spiked proteins, whose amount changes in every comparison, and
`in_h` and `in_l` say whether each converter's results include the protein. A
protein that MSstats could not test, because one condition has no measurement,
is never called significant, whatever its adjusted p-value.

```{r results}
results <- case$results
head(results, 3)
```

For each comparison, the table below counts the proteins called significant
with each column, and the spiked proteins among them.

```{r counts}
counts <- results[, .(area             = sum(sig_h, na.rm = TRUE),
                      area_spiked      = sum(sig_h & spiked, na.rm = TRUE),
                      intensity        = sum(sig_l, na.rm = TRUE),
                      intensity_spiked = sum(sig_l & spiked, na.rm = TRUE)),
                  by = .(comparison = Label)]
counts
```

Over the `r nrow(counts)` comparisons, the hand-written converter, with
`Precursor Area`, calls `r sum(counts$area)` proteins significant,
`r sum(counts$area_spiked)` of them spiked. The LLM-based converter, with
`Intensity`, calls `r sum(counts$intensity)`, `r sum(counts$intensity_spiked)`
of them spiked. The choice of the column decides how much of the true change
the analysis finds.

A call changed when one converter called the protein significant and the
other did not. We count it as near the threshold when the converter that did
not call the protein significant still gave it an adjusted p-value of `NEAR`
or less.

```{r changed}
NEAR <- 0.2
changed <- results[in_h & in_l][xor(sig_h %in% TRUE, sig_l %in% TRUE)]
near <- changed[pmax(adjp_h, adjp_l, na.rm = TRUE) <= NEAR]
c(changed = nrow(changed), near_threshold = nrow(near))
```

Only `r nrow(near)` of the `r nrow(changed)` changed calls were near the
threshold, so the choice of the column does not just move borderline proteins
across it.

# What to check

- Which column the conversion specification reads as `Intensity`. In a
  Proteome Discoverer export, prefer the integrated peak area,
  `Precursor Area`, to the single precursor signal `Intensity`.
- When the export has more than one intensity column, compare them on the
  example rows. Columns whose ratio changes from row to row measure different
  things, and choosing between them changes the results.
- When MSstatsConvert has a converter for the tool, compare the conversion
  specification with the columns that the converter reads by default.
